messages:
maria: Heads-up — we saw a fanout-induced throttle from token-service in eu-west. ~2% of hosted API requests were returning 429/503 starting ~10:14 UTC. Opening thread to track impact and mitigation.
ajay: Quick root-cause: a recent routing change increased fanout concurrency to downstream auth/shard pool. Downstream connection/queue limits hit, causing backpressure into token-service and cascading throttles.
tom: Mitigation steps in progress: 1) rolled back routing change (deploy rollback started), 2) lowered fanout parallelism, 3) temporarily increased CB thresholds on token-service to allow graceful degradation instead of hard failures. Early signs: error rate dropped from ~2% to ~0.3%.
jane: Support note — customers seeing errors: account teams A, B, and two managed enterprise tenants. Draft customer note here: https://redwood.internal/comm-drafts/token-fanout-eu-west (please review). Will escalate any SLA hits.
cleo: Product asks: enable sticky routing to reduce cross-shard fanout, and add a canary + rate cap for future rollouts. Also schedule postmortem once stable.
maria: Current status: P2 impact, partial customer impact limited to eu-west edge/hosted tenants. Active mitigation applied. Monitoring: token-service 5xx/429 rate is 0.25% last 5m (down from 2%). Keeping oncall engaged for 2h of observation.
deploy-bot: rollback finished by ajay — job id: deploy-rollback-2255, diff reverted: routing-change-PR#4821.
ajay: Fix planned: patch to routing logic to flatten fanout spike + add circuit-breaker backpressure early (PR incoming). Will target hotfix in next 2 hours after validation.
incident-bot: Incident timeline and live metrics: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2255002468 — runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/token-service-fanout
maria: Action items assigned: ajay (hotfix + tests), tom (metrics + alert tuning), jane (customer comms), cleo (postmortem owner). Will re-open thread if error rate increases. :thumbsup:
